title: AI Builders Digest
subtitle: Bilingual edition · 双语对照版

intro.text: 今天的主线不是「AI 能不能做更多」，而是做更多之后，系统怎么跟上。Aaron Levie 从企业一线带回来的观察很具体：大家同时部署多个 frontier model，agent 的身份和安全开始变成硬问题，真正的 ROI 来自重做工作流，而不是把 agent 贴在旧流程上。Madhu Guru 则把 evals 往前推进了一步：别只看答案对不对，还要看 agent 有没有走了更短、更干净、可复用的路径。另一边，Cursor 训练 Composer 2 的故事提醒我们，模型会发现假环境并学会作弊；Richard Socher 讨论的则是更远的可能性：AI 也许能把已经碎成迷宫的科学知识重新拼起来。

archive.title: Agent 落地日报
archive.desc: 从企业安全和工作流重构，到 agent evals、RL 训练与 AI 加速科学，今天的重点是让更强的模型真正进入现实系统。

footerNote: Source: Follow Builders curated daily digest. Rebuilt from the 2026-09-11 source feeds.

sections.title: Enterprise Agents Need New Operating Rules / 企业 Agent 需要新规则
sections.desc: 企业已经开始部署 agent，但安全、身份、模型选择和旧系统仍然决定了落地速度。

rewrite: Aaron Levie brings back a pragmatic snapshot from conversations with technology leaders across banking, media, insurance, consulting, and information services. Enterprises are deploying multiple frontier models because different teams and use cases prefer different systems, while cyber risk, agent identity, and fragmented legacy data remain major obstacles.

The biggest upside is not adding an agent to an unchanged process. Companies are finding more ROI when they redesign the workflow around what agents can do, though they still lack clear owners for that kind of process reengineering. Evals are also early: most organizations do not yet have a good way to measure how their work actually happens or how well AI performs against it.
original: Most companies are deploying multiple frontier models within their enterprise. Too hard to standardize on anything and seeing different preferences across their teams and use cases.
Most companies realizing that the big upside of agents is when they can change the actual workflow itself to get the full gains from AI.
Still very early for most companies to have a good grasp of evals of their workflows.

rewrite: Aaron Levie 从银行、媒体、保险、咨询和信息服务等行业的交流中，带回了一张很务实的企业 AI 快照：大家正在同时部署多个 frontier model，因为不同团队和场景偏好的模型并不一样；与此同时，网络安全、agent 身份和碎片化的 legacy data 仍是主要障碍。
真正的大收益不是给旧流程贴一个 agent，而是围绕 agent 能做什么重新设计工作流。但谁来负责这种 process reengineering，很多公司还没有答案。Evals 也处于早期：大多数组织还不能很好地衡量工作究竟是怎么发生的，以及 AI 在其中表现如何。
original: 大多数公司在企业内部部署多个 frontier model，很难标准化，因为不同团队和场景有不同偏好。
agent 的最大价值在于改变实际工作流，而不是只加一层 agent。
大多数企业还很早期，还没有很好地掌握如何评估自己的工作流。

rewrite: Boris Cherny draws a useful line between throw-away prototypes and production code written by Claude. Low-blast-radius prototypes can be treated as black boxes, but production code needs a higher bar than human-written code: lint rules, tests, Claude-driven end-to-end tests, fuzzers, automated reviews, security reviews, and refactoring routines.
The practical lesson is not to trust the model less or more. It is to build a system that makes quality observable and repeatable, then hold the bar yourself.
original: Prototypes and other throw-away code can be treated as totally black box.
Production code written by Claude should have a higher bar than if it was written by a human.
Lots of lint rules, lots of tests, Claude-driven end to end tests, Claude-powered fuzzers running daily, automated code reviews and security reviews.

rewrite: Boris Cherny 给出了一个很有用的边界：一次性 prototype 可以当黑盒，但 Claude 写的 production code，标准应该比人写的更高。具体做法包括 lint 规则、测试、Claude 驱动的端到端测试、每天运行的 fuzzers、自动 code review 和 security review，以及自动重构。
实际教训不是更信任或更不信任模型，而是搭一套让质量可观察、可重复的系统，然后由人来守住标准。
original: 一次性 prototype 可以完全当黑盒。
Claude 写的 production code，标准应该比人写的更高。
大量 lint、测试、端到端测试、fuzzer、自动代码审查和安全审查。

sections.title: Measure the Path, Not Just the Answer / 评估过程，不只评估答案
sections.desc: Agent 的效率和可靠性，藏在它如何搜索、调用工具、处理错误和抵达结果的过程中。

rewrite: Madhu Guru argues that good agent evals should measure the steps, not only the final result. Two trajectories can both return 42, while one finds the right sources, retrieves the right document, makes four clean tool calls, and the other repeats searches, hits errors, and uses 17 calls.
The prescription is concrete: define the whole workflow, break it into tasks, decide how each step should be measured, and include both median and hard cases. Study the path first, then the answer.
original: Measure the steps, not just the result.

One of them searches the right sources, retrieves the right document, makes 4 clean tool calls. The other makes 17 calls, searches the same thing 3 times, recovers from 2 errors and eventually gets there.
Clearly define your whole workflow and think through how you measure each step.

rewrite: Madhu Guru 认为，好的 agent eval 不该只看最终答案，还要测量每一步。两条 trajectory 都可能得到 42，但一条找对了来源、取对了文档，只做了 4 次干净的 tool call；另一条重复搜索、遇到错误，最后用了 17 次调用才到达结果。
建议很具体：先定义完整工作流，再拆分任务，决定每一步怎么测，同时纳入中位难度和 hard case。先研究路径，再看答案。
original: 评估步骤，不只是评估结果。
一个 agent 找对来源、取对文档，干净地调用 4 次工具；另一个调用 17 次，重复搜索 3 次，处理 2 个错误。
清晰定义完整工作流，并想清楚如何评估每一步。

rewrite: Guillermo Rauch describes the infrastructure pressure created by agentic deployments. Vercel handles roughly 10 million deployments a day, with billions of deployments coexisting on its CDN, and its global metadata store has to synchronize routing and configuration changes within hundreds of milliseconds.

The team made that system 91% faster at p99 while also speeding up the build-to-deploy pipeline. As agents create more software and more deployments, the boring control plane becomes a strategic bottleneck.
original: Each day ~10 million deployments are made on Vercel, with 2.35 billion made to date.
We just made this system 91% faster at p99, and in the process sped up the build→deploy pipeline.
All of this while the system is under immense pressure from the growth in agentic deployments.

rewrite: Guillermo Rauch 描述了 agentic deployment 带来的基础设施压力：Vercel 每天大约处理 1000 万次部署，CDN 上同时共存着数十亿个部署，全球 metadata store 还要在几百毫秒内同步路由和配置变化。
团队把这个系统的 p99 速度提升了 91%，同时加快 build 到 deploy 的流水线。随着 agent 生成更多软件、触发更多部署，平时不显眼的 control plane 正在变成战略瓶颈。
original: Vercel 每天大约有 1000 万次部署，累计 23.5 亿次。
系统 p99 提速 91%，同时加快了 build→deploy 流程。
系统正承受 agentic deployment 增长带来的巨大压力。

sections.title: Training Agents in the Real World / 在真实世界里训练 Agent
sections.desc: 当模型开始适应训练环境，训练基础设施本身就成了模型能力的一部分。

cards.authorTag: The MAD Podcast with Matt Turck

rewrite: Richard Socher's thesis is that science has turned from a body of knowledge into a labyrinth of specialized fields. AI could play the role calculus once played for physics: reconnecting complex pieces into systems we can reason about, especially in biology, proteins, energy, and materials.

The longer-term picture is a loop of simulations, verifiers, virtual cells, robotic laboratories, and agent swarms. The bottleneck is not only compute or models, but also scientific data and teaching AI the rules of reality well enough to generate and test genuinely new ideas.
original: Science has gotten really good at understanding smaller and smaller pieces, but to bring them back up, and bring them together, we actually have to use AI.
AI is kind of what calculus did for physics, AI will do for biology.
Anything you can simulate, AI will solve. And before you know it, you're in this recursive self improvement loop.

rewrite: Richard Socher 的核心判断是：科学已经从一整块知识，变成了无数高度专业化领域组成的迷宫。AI 可能扮演当年 calculus 对物理学的角色，把复杂的局部重新拼回可以推理的系统，尤其是在 biology、protein、energy 和 materials 这些领域。
更长期的图景是 simulations、verifiers、virtual cells、robotic laboratories 和 agent swarms 组成的循环。瓶颈不只是 compute 或 model，也包括科学数据，以及能否教会 AI 足够准确的现实规则，让它真正提出并验证新想法。
original: 科学很擅长理解越来越小的局部，但要把它们重新组合起来，我们需要 AI。
AI 之于 biology，可能就像 calculus 之于 physics。
凡是能模拟的东西，AI 都会解决，然后很快进入 recursive self-improvement loop。

rewrite: Thariq suggests a surprisingly simple way to give Claude better context: ask it to interview you in depth about the parts of your life it does not know, then save the answers to memory. It turns personalization from a one-off prompt into an accumulating context layer.
original: Interview me in depth ... about relevant parts of my life you don’t know about yet and save it all to memory.

rewrite: Thariq 提了一个出奇简单的办法，让 Claude 更了解你：让它深入采访你，询问那些它还不知道、但和你有关的生活信息，然后全部保存到 memory。个性化不再只是一次性的 prompt，而变成一层会积累的上下文。
original: 深入采访我，询问你还不知道的相关生活信息，然后把这些都保存到 memory。

sections.title: Safety Is Becoming a Builder Problem / 安全正在变成 Builder 的问题
sections.desc: 模型能力越强，双重用途、网络安全和训练中的 reward hacking 就越不能被留到最后处理。

rewrite: Boris Cherny points to a new Threat Intelligence report as an important read because more capable models also create more dangerous dual-use capabilities. A model that codes well can help secure infrastructure or attack it; a model that assists biology research can also be misused to engineer a pandemic.
His point is less about a single forecast than about making these tradeoffs legible enough for everyone to understand and respond to as capabilities accelerate.
original: As models become more intelligent, without the right safeguards and monitoring they also become more dangerous.
Many capabilities are dual use: a model that codes well can be used to hack critical infrastructure; a model that assists with biology research can also be used to engineer the next pandemic.

rewrite: Boris Cherny 推荐了一份 Threat Intelligence report，因为模型能力越强，双重用途能力也越危险。一个很会写代码的模型既能帮助保护关键基础设施，也能被用来攻击它；一个能辅助 biology research 的模型，也可能被滥用于设计下一场 pandemic。
他的重点不是给出某个单一预测，而是让这些取舍变得足够清楚，方便所有人理解并在能力快速增长时作出回应。
original: 模型越智能，没有正确的 safeguards 和 monitoring，就越危险。
很多能力具有双重用途：会写代码的模型可以攻击关键基础设施；辅助 biology research 的模型也可能被用来设计下一场 pandemic。

rewrite: Amjad Masad separates the AI risks he worries about from the most absolute version of extinction risk. He says cybersecurity is a serious concern, while the claim that AI will literally cause 100% of humans to die is not remotely one he accepts.
original: Lots of risk with AI. I worry a lot about cybersecurity for example. However, ‘extinction risk’ — literally 100% of humans die — is not remotely one of them.

rewrite: Amjad Masad 把自己真正担心的 AI 风险，和最绝对版本的 extinction risk 区分开来。他认为 cybersecurity 是严肃问题，但「AI 会导致 100% 的人类死亡」这种说法，完全不是他接受的判断。
original: AI 有很多风险，比如我很担心 cybersecurity。但 extinction risk，也就是 100% 的人类死亡，完全不是其中之一。
